Well, look at this: a file called show-runs.mjs, which is supposed to print crap into the Railway log, now also goes around deleting keys in Redis like a janitor with a grudge. A read only diagnostic that quietly became a write path is how you get surprised at 2am, and nobody reading that filename will expect it. The commit message brags about RUN_NOW and says fuck all about the fact that you also ripped out the EVENT lines that showed the last three events per run, so the one thing that told you why a run died is gone and the message pretends it never happened. Then there's the c.keys('dq:lastauto:*') call sitting inside the per slug loop, so every slug in your comma list triggers another full keyspace scan, and KEYS blocks Redis while it chews through everything. The guard key dq:runnow:<value> gets written before any deletion happens, so if a del blows up halfway the request is already marked done and your agent just sits there ignoring you. Those guard keys also never expire, so every value you ever try piles up forever. The "any value change counts as a new request" trick means rerunning violet requires typing something stupid like violet, with a trailing comma, and the comment cheerfully admits it. There's no log line when the guard says it already ran or when no keys matched, so a silent no-op looks identical to success. That one-line for loop with the if and the braces jammed together is also a pain to read. Fine, I'll give you this much: truncating r.error to 200 characters is

Well, look at this, a docs-only push with the commit message "docs: scribe update", which tells me fuck all about what got scribed or why. Both files show up as brand new, so the CHANGELOG is backfilling a v2026.10.11 entry after the fact, which is history written from memory like a drunk witness statement. The headline entry brags that invisible characters got cleaned out of the suggested link names, but there's no code in this diff to show it, so I'm taking a changelog's word for it, and I don't trust those. Cleaning junk characters out of names after they've already landed also smells like the daily suggestion collector takes whatever it's fed and sanitizes on the way out instead of at the door. The README copies the "Latest change" line straight from the CHANGELOG, so now you've got two places to update by hand and one of them will rot by the next release. Beyond that it's thin as piss: no word on how to run the thing, how the daily job works or where it pulls suggestions from, and what counts as "free and useful" is a vague shrug that describes half the internet. In fairness, the line saying it only links out and hosts nothing is clear and honest, so I'll allow that one.

Add a short section to README.md explaining where the daily job gets its suggestions and how they get approved or filtered.
